candidates.exact_span: Placement of sewage sludge shall not contaminate an aquifer. This shall be demonstrated through one of the following:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether aquifer-protection compliance must be shown by groundwater monitoring or may be satisfied by certification affects whether groundwater monitoring was required and how absent groundwater results should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: a. Results of a ground-water monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water scientist.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting this demonstration path establishes a groundwater monitoring obligation; if evidence instead reflects the certification path, applicability of required monitoring and the meaning of missing groundwater data change.

candidates.exact_span: b. A certification by a qualified ground-water scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If this alternative is the operative compliance path, groundwater monitoring may not be required, changing monitoring-obligation findings and whether missing groundwater data indicates a required-but-unmet obligation or a documented no-data state.

candidates.exact_span: the concentration of methane gas in air in any structure within the surface disposal site shall not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets an enforceable numeric methane limit (25% of LEL) for structures; different readings of the limit basis or active-period scope change which reported measurements are compared and whether they exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a separate enforceable numeric methane limit (100% of LEL) at the property line; interpretation of location, active-period timing, or LEL basis changes limit applicability and exceedance determinations.

Establishes a continuous methane monitoring requirement tied to the numeric limits; interpretation of what counts as continuous monitoring affects whether monitoring was required and how gaps or missing methane data are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a one-time TCLP testing obligation with a permit-effective-date window; whether FY2025 falls inside that window or the test was already satisfied changes required-monitoring findings and how absent TCLP results are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when TCLP sampling is required relative to treatment and off-site transfer; different readings of final treatment or leaving the site affect whether a monitoring event was required for a given period and how missing results are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested at the frequency show below in Element 2, Section I.D. for PCBs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporates PCB testing frequency by cross-reference; resolving that external frequency determines whether PCB monitoring was required in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Any sludge exceeding a concentration of 50 mg/Kg shall not be surface disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States an enforceable numeric PCB concentration threshold; interpretation of units, sample basis, or whether a reported PCB value exceeds 50 mg/Kg changes applicable limit and exceedance outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is disposed of in a surface disposal site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements unless sewage sludge is placed on an active surface disposal site, and is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Chooses among Class A, Class B, and daily-cover (Class C) compliance paths with different numeric and monitoring expectations; whether the daily-cover exception applies changes applicable limits, required monitoring, and how missing pathogen evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: When reporting on the DMR, list pathogen reduction level attained as A, B, or C (daily cover).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links reported DMR entries to the operative pathogen compliance regime; interpretation of reported A/B/C levels affects which monitoring and limit framework applies and how absent or ambiguous DMR pathogen data are read.

candidates.exact_span: When reporting how compliance was met, list Alternative 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 for Class A, or Alternative Number 1, 2, 3, or 4 for Class B, on DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: DMR alternative selection identifies which specific Class A or B demonstration method—and its associated numeric criteria—was used; different alternative interpretations change applicable limits, monitoring proof requirements, and missing-evidence handling.

candidates.exact_span: All 6 alternatives require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a numeric fecal-coliform limit for Class A alternatives; interpretation of dry-weight basis, MPN units, or whether the Salmonella alternative applies changes which numeric limit governs and exceedance findings. The segment truncates before completing the Salmonella criterion, leaving applicability uncertain.
